facts.text: You must have a CDL to drive any single vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating of 26,001 pounds or more.
You must have a CDL to drive a combination vehicle with a gross combination weight rating of 26,001 pounds or more, when the vehicle being towed is rated over 10,000 pounds.
You must have a CDL to drive a vehicle designed to carry 16 or more passengers, including the driver.
You must have a CDL to drive any size vehicle that needs hazardous material placards, or that carries a material listed as a select agent or toxin.
Class A is a combination of vehicles with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more, when the towed vehicle or vehicles are rated over 10,000 pounds.
Class B is a single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more, or such a vehicle towing another vehicle rated at 10,000 pounds or less.
Class C is a single vehicle under 26,001 pounds GVWR, included in the CDL programme only when it carries 16 or more passengers including the driver, or needs hazmat placards.
A Class A licence also lets you drive Class B and Class C vehicles, and a Class B licence also lets you drive Class C vehicles.
There are six kinds of CDL endorsement: double and triple trailers (T), tank vehicle (N), passenger (P), hazardous materials (H), school bus (S), and the combination of tank and hazmat (X).
Only three endorsements can be added to a commercial learner's permit: passenger (P), school bus (S) and tank vehicle (N).
A tank vehicle endorsement is needed for a tank with an individual rated capacity over 119 gallons and a total rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more.

cards.q: What single vehicle weight rating needs a CDL?
cards.a: A GVWR of 26,001 lb or more.

cards.q: What combination weight ratings need a CDL?
cards.a: A GCWR of 26,001 lb or more, with the towed vehicle rated over 10,000 lb.

cards.q: How many passengers make a vehicle a CDL vehicle?
cards.a: 16 or more, including the driver.

cards.q: Define a Class A vehicle.
cards.a: A combination with a GCWR of 26,001 lb or more, towing a unit rated over 10,000 lb.

cards.q: Define a Class B vehicle.
cards.a: A single vehicle of 26,001 lb GVWR or more, or one towing a unit rated 10,000 lb or less.

cards.q: Define a Class C vehicle.
cards.a: A vehicle under 26,001 lb that carries 16+ people including the driver, or needs hazmat placards.

cards.q: Which classes may a Class A holder drive?
cards.a: Class A, B and C.

cards.q: Which endorsements can go on a commercial learner's permit?
cards.a: Passenger (P), school bus (S) and tank vehicle (N) only.

cards.q: What tank capacity needs the N endorsement?
cards.a: An individual tank over 119 gallons, with 1,000 gallons or more in total.

exam.q: Which combination needs a Class A licence?
choices: A GCWR of 26,001 lb with a 12,000 lb trailer
A GCWR of 24,000 lb with a 12,000 lb trailer
A GCWR of 30,000 lb with an 8,000 lb trailer
A single truck of 30,000 lb GVWR
exam.why: Class A needs a GCWR of 26,001 lb or more AND a towed unit rated over 10,000 lb.

exam.q: A 15-passenger van weighing 9,000 lb needs which licence?
choices: No CDL for the passenger count alone
exam.why: A CDL is needed at 16 or more people including the driver, so 15 is below the limit.

facts.text: The general knowledge test is taken by every CDL applicant.
You must take the air brakes test if your vehicle has air brakes, and air over hydraulic brakes count as air brakes.
The combination vehicles test is required if you want to drive combination vehicles, which includes every Class A driver.
The hazardous materials test needs entry level driver training and a Transportation Security Administration background check.
For a Class A licence the manual says to study sections 1, 2, 3, 6, 11, 12 and 13, and section 5 as well if you will drive a vehicle with air brakes.

cards.q: Which knowledge test does every CDL applicant take?
cards.a: The general knowledge test.

cards.q: Do air over hydraulic brakes count as air brakes for the test?
cards.a: Yes. You must take the air brakes test.

cards.q: Which knowledge tests does a Class A driver with air brakes take?
cards.a: General knowledge, combination vehicles, and air brakes.

cards.q: Which manual sections should a Class A applicant with air brakes study?

exam.q: Your tractor has air over hydraulic brakes. Which test must you take?
exam.why: Air over hydraulic brakes count as air brakes, so the air brakes test is required.

facts.text: The skills test has three parts: vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, and on-road driving.
You must take the three skills test parts in order, and you must pass each part before you go on to the next.
You must take the skills test in the type of vehicle you want to be licensed for.
A vehicle with marked or labelled components cannot be used for the CDL skills test.
In the vehicle inspection test you must point to or touch each item, name it, and tell the examiner what you would inspect and why.
In the basic vehicle control test you move the vehicle forward, backward and turn it inside a marked area, and the examiner tells you how each exercise is done.
You can take the skills test after you pass the required knowledge tests and finish entry level driver training.

cards.q: What are the three parts of the CDL skills test, in order?
cards.a: Vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, then on-road driving.

cards.q: Can you take the skills test parts in any order?
cards.a: No. They are taken in order, and each must be passed before the next.

cards.q: Which vehicle must you use for the skills test?
cards.a: The type of vehicle you want the licence for.

cards.q: Can a vehicle with labelled parts be used for the skills test?
cards.a: No. Marked or labelled components are not allowed.

cards.q: What must you do for each item in the vehicle inspection test?
cards.a: Point to or touch it, name it, and say what you inspect and why.

exam.q: You fail the basic vehicle control part. What happens next?
choices: You go on to the on-road test
You cannot go on to the on-road test
You get the licence with a restriction
exam.why: Each part must be passed before the next one, so a failed part stops the test there.

exam.q: During the inspection test, what must you do at each item?
choices: Point to or touch it, name it, and explain what and why
exam.why: The test needs you to point to or touch the item, name it, and explain the check.

facts.text: Utah requires at least one year of experience as a licensed driver before you can apply for a CDL.
Utah requires your driver licence and your current Medical Examiner's Certificate, form MCSA-5876, also called the medical certificate or DOT card.
You must give up your driver licence to the Division when you get your Utah commercial driver instruction permit, and the permit then lets you drive your own vehicle.
A CDL applicant under 21 years of age cannot get the passenger, school bus or hazardous materials endorsements.

cards.q: How much driving experience does Utah require before a CDL?
cards.a: At least one year as a licensed driver.

cards.q: Which medical form must a Utah CDL applicant provide?
cards.a: The current Medical Examiner's Certificate, MCSA-5876 (the DOT card).

cards.q: What happens to your driver licence when you get a CDIP in Utah?
cards.a: You surrender it to the Division, and the CDIP lets you drive your own vehicle.

cards.q: Which endorsements are barred under age 21 in Utah?
cards.a: Passenger, school bus and hazardous materials.

exam.q: A 20-year-old Utah applicant may NOT get which endorsement?
exam.why: Under 21, the passenger, school bus and hazmat endorsements are not available.
